sub_theme: A Village Far Away: Introducing Our Contrasting Locality

lessons.title: Non-Fiction: A Village in India
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about a contrasting locality from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about the village.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of the village and predict what life might be like there.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about a village in India (e.g. Chembakolli), an approach widely used to teach contrasting localities.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
resources_needed: Non-fiction text/resource about a village in India
key_questions: What is this village like?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about the village.
lessons.home_link: Find India on a map or globe with your family.

lessons.title: Number Recap: Counting and Comparing to 100
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and compare numbers to 100 confidently.
success_criteria: I can count to 100.
I can compare two numbers.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate counting and comparing numbers to 100 using a 100 square.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a mixed counting/comparing consolidation activity.
key_questions: What comes after 78?
Which number is greater?
lessons.assessment_notes: Consolidation check on number skills mid-year — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting and comparing numbers together.

lessons.title: Locating India on a World Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to locate India on a world map and name its continent.
success_criteria: I can find India on a world map.
I can say which continent it's in.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model locating India on a world map, identifying it's in Asia.
lessons.independent_task: Children locate and label India on a world map outline, noting the continent.
key_questions: Where is India?
Which continent is it part of?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge, beginning the contrasting locality study — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Find India on a map or globe together.

lessons.title: Writing About the Village
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about the village using expanded noun phrases.
success_criteria: I can describe the village.
I can use an expanded noun phrase.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about the village from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about the village using an expanded noun phrase.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing the village.
key_questions: What does the village look like?
Can you use an expanded noun phrase?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied noun phrases

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing and grammar application — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Describe the village to your family.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction Recap to 100
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add and subtract two-digit numbers confidently.
success_criteria: I can add two-digit numbers.
I can subtract two-digit numbers.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate two-digit addition and subtraction, including crossing tens.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a mixed addition/subtraction consolidation activity.
key_questions: What strategy will you use?
Can you solve this mentally?
lessons.assessment_notes: Consolidation check on addition/subtraction — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate progress in addition and subtraction.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition and subtraction over the week.

lessons.title: Homes in the Village
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of homes in the village.
success_criteria: I can describe a home in the village.
I can compare it to my own home.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children's own homes are like.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss features of homes in the village (e.g. materials used, layout).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare a village home to their own home, recording similarities and differences.
key_questions: What is this home like?
How is it similar to or different from yours?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative geographical thinking about human features — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap village vs own home comparisons.
lessons.home_link: Describe your own home to your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Village-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read village-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read village words.
I can read a sentence about the village.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to village-themed words (e.g. 'field', 'market', 'well').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading village-themed words over the week.

lessons.title: Village Data: Interpreting a Pictogram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to interpret a pictogram about the village.
success_criteria: I can read a pictogram.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model interpreting a pictogram about the village (e.g. types of crops grown).
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions using a village-themed pictogram.
key_questions: Which crop is grown most?
How many more of this than that?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record data interpretation applied to a geography context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Interpret a pictogram together if you find one in a book.

lessons.title: How Do People in the Village Get Food?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how people in the village get their food.
success_criteria: I can describe how food is grown/gathered.
I can compare it to how we get food.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how children's families get food (shops, supermarkets).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how many villagers grow their own food or farm locally.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare getting food in the village to their own experience, recording similarities/differences.
key_questions: How do people in the village get food?
How is this different from how you get food?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative human geography understanding — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about where your family's food comes from.

lessons.title: Asking Questions About the Village
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to formulate relevant questions about a topic.
success_criteria: I can ask a relevant question.
I can explain what I want to find out.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts learned about the village so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model forming relevant questions about the village to research further.
lessons.independent_task: Children formulate 2-3 questions they'd like answered about the village.
key_questions: What would you like to know?
Is this a relevant question?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note questioning skill, a Year 2 spoken language objective — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.home_link: Research one of your questions with your family if possible.

lessons.title: Village Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a village context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a village context (e.g. crops harvested).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve village-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
key_questions: How many altogether?
How many are left?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a village word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Weather and Climate in India
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe the climate of the region where the village is located.
success_criteria: I can describe the climate there.
I can compare it to the UK's climate.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the climate of the region (warm, monsoon season), comparing to the UK's climate.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the village's climate to the UK's, recording similarities/differences.
key_questions: What is the climate like there?
How is it different from the UK?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note climate comparison, a key contrasting locality skill — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Compare today's UK weather to what you've learned about India's climate.

lessons.title: A Village Far Away Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the contrasting village.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about the village, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What is a home in the village like?
Why might climate affect what people grow?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on village facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Number and Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply number and data handling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can add and subtract confidently.
I can interpret a pictogram.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of number and data handling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: number, data handling.
key_questions: What is the total?
What does the pictogram show?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 18 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N2/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition and subtraction over the weekend.

lessons.title: Introducing Our Village Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise initial learning about the contrasting village.
success_criteria: I can name a fact about the village.
I can say one question I still have.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising this introductory week's learning about the village, previewing next week's deeper comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'A Village Far Away' display combining maps, facts, and questions from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about the village so far?
What do you want to find out next week?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note initial locality knowledge, setting up direct comparison next week — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'A Village Far Away' display so far.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the village this week with your family.
